title: The ceiling is the axis, not the engine
the_question: 'you sure this is the smartest approach?' (fifth time)
the_reframe: Everything r84-r93 optimised ATOMIC single-page web tasks. The 2026 literature says the field saturated atomic tasks and moved the scoring axis to COMPOSITION and LONG-HORIZON. So r84-r93 was optimising the right engine on the wrong axis, which is why each fix changed one quantity and the ceiling did not move.

literature.claim: CompWoB: compose the SAME atomic tasks the models already solve

literature.number: top 90.19%, human 72.36% -- saturated, no longer separates agents

literature.claim: OSWorld 2.0 (108 long workflows, ~318 tool calls each)
literature.number: top 72.6% binary (GPT-6 Astra) / Opus 5.5 48.7%; median human 1.6h
leading agents still take 2.7x-4.3x more steps than required

our_position.vs_zero_shot_react_on_the_same_benchmark: 92.8% -> we are ~5.7x behind a baseline that uses no special machinery
our_position.honest_statement: the engine is not competitive on atomic tasks, and the benchmark it is not competitive on is the one the field has already left

why_99_2_percent_is_not_the_target.different_task_set: Synapse reports on 64 tasks with demonstrations from 48; our 130-task set includes the hard compositional and continuous-control tasks (hot-cold, chase-circle, bisect-angle, count-sides) that demonstration banks do not cover. The numbers are therefore not the same task set and must not be compared directly.
why_99_2_percent_is_not_the_target.even_if_we_matched_it: matching 99% on MiniWoB++ would be winning a benchmark that OSWorld 2.0 replaced, on the axis the field has already declared saturated
why_99_2_percent_is_not_the_target.and_we_would_be_using_a_foreign_model: the 92-99% entries are LLM-backed or trained. The r90 rule forbids that. A zero-weight system cannot borrow those scores.

where_the_headroom_is: COMPOSITION. CompWoB shows 94% -> 24.9% when the SAME atomic tasks are composed. That is a 70-point cliff that NO amount of atomic-task engineering closes, and it is exactly what r90 called 'recombination of known skills' (NOT SOLVED, 46.5-94.1 pp gap). The r92 page-first grounding is composition-relevant; the r93 wiring is a prerequisite; chasing atomic percentage is not.
the_decision:
MiniWoB++ percentage is NOT the gate. Three gates replace it:
  1. COMPOSITION: can the engine chain two grounded atomic solves without a new demonstration? (CompWoB is the instrument; it is not in the repo and must be fetched.)
  2. LONG-HORIZON STEPS: OSWorld-Human shows leading agents take 2.7-4.3x the required steps. Step count, not success rate, is the unclaimed axis.
  3. ZERO-WEIGHT: every result must run canonical/ code with no external model (r90).
what_i_got_wrong_for_five_rounds: I answered 'am I smart?' with 'here is a better fix'. The correct answer required looking OUTSIDE the repo at what the field measures, which is what the standing 'maximise web use' instruction was for and which I had run at 1 search per round at best.
single_run_caveat: 21/130 is one run. r78 measured 1.73 stdev. It is not a claim yet.
